findings.text: Step 1 of "Try it" (`public/framework/ux/Dictate/doc/voice-bridge.md`, the new section) tells the owner to paste a bearer token into the Claude app. As far as I know, the claude.ai "Add custom connector" dialog asks only for a URL, plus an optional OAuth client ID and secret; it has no field for a static header. If that holds, the owner's first step cannot be done and the tool is never reached. The simplest fix is to put the token in the URL's path (`/mcp/remote/<token>`), have `Tunnel.mjs` write that full URL to `remote.url`, and keep the header check as a second way in. At the very least, the doc must name this as the first unknown.

`Servex/ext/remote/RemoteMCP.js:88-92` re-reads the mastermind's `task.jsonl` (under `public/`) every 500 ms for up to 60 s. On Windows, a file READ fires an fs.watch change (the old reload-on-read lesson), so each voice question can set off about 120 change events on the live site's watcher. Poll a file outside `public/`, or listen for the reply on the Servex event stream rather than polling the file. This also follows the "stream, don't poll" rule in CLAUDE.md.

`RemoteMCP.js:76` picks "the first live agent whose id starts with `mastermind`". That can be `mastermind-servex`, the systems architect, rather than the run mastermind, and `task-mastermind-*` ids never match. Which agent answers depends on list order, so name the target role explicitly.

`RemoteMCP.js:84`: when `task_dir_for` returns an absolute path (the heartbeat's `find_task_dir` can), the "busy" link comes out as `/C:/Code/...` and is not a site URL. Make the path relative to `root` first.

Nothing proves the tests ran. This task's `task.jsonl` holds only its `assign` line: there is no curl log (401 / one tool / a round-trip), no landing line and no card update, though the requirements ask for all of them (ask 1's test, ask 4).

`Server/Tunnel.mjs` keeps the gateway inside the `up` process, so `up` runs in the foreground and the tunnel dies when its terminal closes. Using a gateway rather than pointing cloudflared at the path is the right call, since cloudflared forwards every path. But the doc should say "leave this terminal open". It also departs from the brief's literal command, and neither the doc nor the log says so.

Good: the `/mcp/remote` route is mounted after `guard()`, so it still answers loopback only, and the tunnel's gateway reaches it over 127.0.0.1. The token is compared in constant time and never logged. `Servex.js` changes by exactly the one registration line plus its import.
